commit.message:
DATEVALUE: roll the date over when the time part reaches 24 hours like Excel (#1379)

`parse_datevalue_text` in `base/src/functions/date_and_time.rs` cut the
text at the first `T` or space and threw the time part away, so
`DATEVALUE("2026-01-01 24:00:00")` and `DATEVALUE("2026-01-01 25:00:00")`
returned 46023 where Excel returns 46024.

I keep the time part and read it with a new helper `whole_days_in_time`.
It accepts `H:M`, `H:M:S` and `H:M:S.f` with non negative integer hours
and minutes, returns the whole days in that time and returns 0 for any
other text (AM/PM, empty, unparseable), so every input outside the issue
keeps its old result. `parse_datevalue_text` adds those days to the serial
before the `MINIMUM_DATE_SERIAL_NUMBER..=MAXIMUM_DATE_SERIAL_NUMBER`
check, so a rollover past 9999-12-31 is still an error. DATEDIF reads text
dates through the same function and rolls over with it. TIMEVALUE and the
1900 leap day special case are unchanged.

The unit test `base/src/test/test_datevalue_rollover.rs` covers the issue
rows, 23:59:59 without rollover, the ISO `T` form and DATEDIF. The
workbook attached to #1379 goes into `xlsx/tests/calc_tests/DATE_AND_TIME`
unchanged, so the generated xlsx test compares B2 to B5 with the values
Excel saved in it.

`whole_days_in_time` reuses `squeeze_separator_spaces` from #1485 on
the time part, with `:` as the separator.

Before the fix, on main 03beb38e with only the new test and workbook
added.

```
$ cargo test -p ironcalc_base --lib test_datevalue_rollover
panicked at base/src/test/test_datevalue_rollover.rs:19:5
  left: "46023"
 right: "46024"
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 2740 filtered out

$ cargo test -p ironcalc --test generated_tests issue_1
test test_calc_DATE_AND_TIME_DATEVALUE_issue_1379 ... FAILED
  DATEVALUE!B2  Excel: 46024 (number)  IronCalc: 46023 (number)
  DATEVALUE!B3  Excel: 46024 (number)  IronCalc: 46023 (number)
test result: FAILED. 2 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 233 filtered out
```

After the fix.

```
$ cargo test -p ironcalc_base --lib test_datevalue_rollover
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 2740 filtered out

$ cargo test -p ironcalc --test generated_tests issue_1
test test_calc_DATE_AND_TIME_TIMEVALUE_issue_1402 ... ok
test test_calc_DATE_AND_TIME_DATEVALUE_issue_1380 ... ok
test test_calc_DATE_AND_TIME_DATEVALUE_issue_1379 ... ok

$ cargo test -p ironcalc_base -p ironcalc
ironcalc_base lib   test result: ok. 2733 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored
generated_tests     test result: ok. 236 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
other targets       test result: ok, 0 failed (doc tests 23 and 3 passed)

$ cargo fmt -- --check
exit 0

$ cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -W clippy::unwrap_used -W clippy::expect_used -W clippy::panic -D warnings
Finished `dev` profile, no warnings
```

Excel's result for 48 hours and more isn't in the issue, so whole days
past 24 hours follow the same arithmetic and have no Excel value behind
them. Not run are the wasm, Python and Node.js binding tests and the
webapp npm checks.
